entities.summary: Herman I, Margrave of Baden, played a pivotal role in the 11th-century politics of the Holy Roman Empire. He was a key figure in the negotiations leading to the Treaty of Verona in 1074, which secured the Margraviate of Verona for his line. As the titular Margrave of Verona, Herman I's influence extended to the surrounding territories, including the Duchy of Swabia and the Bishopric of Strasbourg. His descendants would go on to shape the history of the Margraviate of Baden for centuries to come. Herman I's legacy is also reflected in the numerous historical records of his reign, including the Annales Bertiniani, which provide valuable insights into the politics and society of the time. The 2020 exhibition at the Historisches Museum der Stadt Freiburg-Müritz showcased the significance of Herman I's Margraviate, highlighting the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that defined the Holy Roman Empire during this period. Herman I's contributions to the development of the Margraviate of Baden are also reflected in the contemporary accounts of his contemporaries, such as the 12th-century historian Otto of Freising. Herman I's reign was marked by a series of strategic marriages and alliances, which cemented his position as a powerful player in the Holy Roman Empire. His descendants would go on to play a significant role in shaping the history of the region, including the founding of the City of Baden in 1805.
